correctness.rationale: For arbitrary real polynomials f,g of total degree ≤2, all four lines of Q=[-1/2,1/2]^2 are invariant. If finitely many boundary equilibria, each open edge contributes ≤2 and four fixed corners give N≤12. On an oriented invariant circle, each full hyperbolic sink is attracting from both adjacent arcs, requiring a separate intervening zero; 2S≤N, so N≤11 implies S≤5. If N=12, each edge has two distinct quadratic roots, exactly one tangential sink per edge. Opposite horizontal restricted quadratics share the x² leading coefficient and opposite vertical ones share y² coefficient, fixing simultaneous end orientations; at most one corner can attract along both incident edges. Hence ≤4 open-edge plus 1 corner sinks. For an identically stationary edge, hyperbolic sinks persist under generic coefficient perturbation, reducing to finite case. Independent direct evaluation of stated explicit f,g yields horizontal roots ≈(-0.204024,0.404024) and vertical roots ≈(0.0351978,0.3648022), 12 boundary hyperbolic equilibria classified as 5 sinks, 6 saddles, 1 source; all signs are strict, so open coefficient realization. Source exact checker check_boundary_sinks.py uses rational quadratic fields to certify witness; finite check not used for infinite coefficient bound.

evidence: The published 2026-11-08 result proves at most 11 total boundary equilibria within the Grau–Szántó six-parameter class; it is not a theorem for arbitrary quadratic f and g, where the present witness has 12 boundary equilibria.

value.rationale: Five is a sharp boundary capacity for a natural broad quartic invariant-square model. It distinguishes full-plane stability from one-dimensional tangential attraction and from total equilibrium counts, with synchronized opposite-edge leading coefficients producing a genuine structural sharp bound. Useful when examining boundary attractor configurations in planar polynomial dynamics; not an arbitrary unmotivated sample.

limitations: Finite witness sign evaluation does not independently establish the all-coefficient theorem; this follows from the inspected sign/alternation proof.
